stories.headline: Nvidia stops H200 sales in China a day after a US rule on remote chip access
stories.dek: Jefferies says the rule could cut $44B to $62B from next year's data center sales. Nvidia says backlog covers it.

facts.text: Acting CEO Colette Kress said Nvidia will no longer sell H200 chips in China, ending a deal that let the US collect a 25% tariff
Commerce issued a rule so chip export limits can't be bypassed through remote access to data centers in third countries

Q3 revenue, up 103% from a year ago; Nvidia's outlook assumes no data center compute revenue from China

open.label: Open question
open.text: How much demand is tied to China. Critics put it as high as 20% of revenue, and Nvidia stopped breaking out its Singapore sales.

chart.note: Derived: Q3 data center revenue of $107.6B times four. Jefferies' range is for next year.

stories.headline: Spy chief ties an NSA outage to PHP patching; other outages had different stated causes
stories.dek: AI helped find last month's critical PHP flaws. Claims that AI-driven patching caused the week's outages lack public support.

facts.text: DNI Jay Clayton said patching after a PHP vulnerability kept NSA systems from coming back up, and saw no sign of a coordinated attack
critical PHP flaws were disclosed after Wiz found them with AI help, including Google's Gemini 4 Argon
of websites run PHP, Wiz says; the NSA told operators to patch fast or take systems offline
FAA ground stop; its chief said there was zero evidence of AI involvement. Microsoft and JPMorgan Chase blamed software bugs

open.label: Unproven
open.text: Three anonymous sources told the Washington Sun that bank executives and NSA officials blamed the outages on patching AI-found flaws. The public record doesn't show that beyond the NSA.

stories.headline: Employers blamed AI for 1 in 5 US job cuts this year, but under 3% in October
stories.dek: Goldman expects a low-hire, low-fire market for another year, with AI displacement growing later.

facts.text: announced US job cuts cited AI through October, about 20% of 617,189 (Challenger)
cuts cited AI in October, under 3% of the month, against about 40% in May
of workers could be displaced during the AI transition, Goldman economist Joseph Briggs estimated
of payrolls laid off in September, 1.6 million people, while hires ran at 5.4 million (JOLTS)

open.label: Caveat
open.text: Challenger counts the reasons employers give, not what drove each cut. A Lightcast economist says labor data doesn't show mass replacement.

correction.text: We said 22% of this year's US job cuts cited AI, about 121,000 jobs. The 22% share ran through August. Through October, the 121,401 AI-cited cuts were about 20% of all announced cuts.
